A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TwigVLM research. Their main text, appendices A–D, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. Visual inspection resolved content missing from text extraction, and relocated material was matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original accuracy and generation-speed experiments, architectural ablations, token-acceptance measurements and qualitative analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds Qwen2.5-VL experiments, training-data sensitivity results and memory measurements.

M1.justification: The twig architecture, autoregressive training objective, twig-guided pruning, FinalWipe and self-speculative decoding remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 is identical; applying the method to Qwen does not introduce a documented procedural adaptation.

E1.justification: v2 adds MAmmoTH-VL single-image instruction data for training the Qwen twig, including a stated 5M-example subset. The existing LLaVA-665K and VideoInstruct-100K training coverage and image/video evaluation tasks remain.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in all matched benchmark, ablation and qualitative comparisons. The added Qwen experiment uses the already evaluated FastV method; newly cited AuroraCap and Imp are not added experimental baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds a Qwen2.5-VL-7B configuration with 1,280 original visual tokens and retained averages of 426, 284 and 142. New supplementary protocols vary training-data fractions across 25–100% and measure VRAM usage. Existing training settings, pruning defaults and accuracy/speed metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B.2 adds two targeted analyses: training-data sensitivity for LLaVA and Qwen (Figure 7), and model-weight versus inference memory costs (Table 11). The original component ablations, token-acceptance analysis and qualitative case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new experiments continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Matched earlier results remain unchanged. New Table 9 reports, at 88.9% pruning, Qwen-based TwigVLM RelAcc/RelSpd of 91.0%/152.3%, versus FastV's 79.1%/104.3%. Figure 7 and Table 11 add data-efficiency and memory outcomes; these are new results, not improvements over matched v1 settings.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(6), including the token-selection and retained-token definitions, are unchanged. Neither version adds formal assumptions, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains a learned twig combining better token pruning with faster long-response decoding. The headline 96% accuracy retention at 88.9% pruning and approximately 1.54-times generation speed remain unchanged; Qwen supplies additional support for the existing generality claim.

C2.justification: v2 refines the explanation of diminishing accuracy returns with twig depth and adds interpretations of data efficiency and deployment costs. Its memory analysis discusses additional weight storage versus pruning savings; Table 11 shows slightly increased inference memory for LLaVA-1.5 but reduced memory for LLaVA-NeXT.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the future-code promise with a repository address and documents Qwen training on 5M examples for 12 hours using eight A100 GPUs. Appendix A also changes the reported LLaVA training estimates from about 1/12 hours to 10/100 GPU-hours, without establishing a changed training procedure.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to AuroraCap, MAmmoTH-VL and Imp, and removes MiniGPT-4. These are limited literature updates; the positioning relative to visual-token pruning and collaborative decoding remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized introduction and explanatory edits, updates author information, adds acknowledgments and divides Appendix B into performance comparisons and ablation studies. The main narrative and section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the Qwen and memory tables and a two-panel data-efficiency figure. It restyles Figure 6 and relocates Algorithm 1 and existing appendix tables. Earlier qualitative figures are retained as Figures 8–9 after renumbering.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the Qwen evaluation, data-efficiency experiment and memory accounting provide useful additional evidence about generality and practical costs. The code pointer also improves reproducibility information. These are incremental gains; some new settings remain unclear, including those needed to reconcile the Qwen speed measurements in Figure 7 with Table 9.
